Port Hacking, NSW]] '''''Eucalyptus tricarpa''''', commonly known as '''red ironbark'''{{cite web |title=''Eucalyptus tricarpa'' |url=https://apps.lucidcentral.org/euclid/text/entities/eucalyptus_tricarpa.htm |publisher=Euclid: Centre for Australian National Biodiversity Research |access-date=28 May 2020}} or '''mugga ironbark''',{{cite web |last1=Hill |first1=Ken |title=''Eucalyptus tricarpa'' |url=http://plantnet.rbgsyd.nsw.gov.au/cgi-bin/NSWfl.pl?page=nswfl&lvl=sp&name=Eucalyptus~tricarpa |publisher=Royal Botanic Garden Sydney |access-date=11 January 2020}} is a species of tree that is [[Endemism|endemic]] to south-eastern Australia. It has thick, rough [[ironbark]] on the trunk and branches, lance-shaped adult leaves, flower buds usually in groups of three, white flowers and cylindrical or spherical fruit. ==Description== ''Eucalyptus tricarpa'' is a tree that typically grows to a height of {{cvt|35|m}} and forms a [[lignotuber]]. It has thick rough, reddish brown to black ironbark on the trunk and branches. Young plants and [[coppice]] regrowth have green to greyish, elliptical to lance-shaped leaves that are {{cvt|40-110|mm}} long and {{cvt|13-30|mm}} wide and [[Petiole (botany)|petiolate]]. Adult leaves are arranged alternately, the same shade of green to greyish green on both sides, lance-shaped to curved, {{cvt|80-220|mm}} long and {{cvt|10-26|mm}} wide, tapering to a petiole {{cvt|10-30|mm}} long. The flower buds are arranged in leaf [[wikt:axil|axil]]s in groups of three, sometimes seven, on an unbranched [[Peduncle (botany)|peduncle]] {{cvt|8-15|mm}} long, the individual buds on [[Pedicel (botany)|pedicels]] {{cvt|5-18|mm}} long. Mature buds are oval, {{cvt|10-15|mm}} long and {{cvt|6-9|mm}} wide with a conical to beaked [[Operculum (botany)|operculum]]. Flowering occurs from February to November and the flowers are white or pale pink. The fruit is a woody cylindrical to shortened spherical [[Capsule (botany)|capsule]] {{cvt|8-13|mm}} long and {{cvt|8-15|mm}} wide with the valves enclosed below the rim.{{cite web |last1=Brooker |first1=M. Ian H. |last2=Slee |first2=Andrew V. |title=''Eucalyptus tricarpa'' |url=https://vicflora.rbg.vic.gov.au/flora/taxon/46b30d64-1f21-4d71-a770-027910050d6c |publisher=Royal Botanic Gardens Victoria |access-date=11 January 2020}}{{cite web |last1=Chippendale |first1=George M. |title=''Eucalyptus sideroxylon'' subsp. ''tricarpa'' |url=https://profiles.ala.org.au/opus/foa/profile/Eucalyptus%20sideroxylon%20subsp.%20tricarpa |publisher=Australian Biological Resources Study, Department of the Environment and Energy, Canberra |access-date=11 January 2020}} ==Taxonomy and naming== The red ironbark was first formally described in 1962 by [[Lawrence Alexander Sidney Johnson|Lawrie Johnson]] who gave it the name ''Eucalyptus sideroxylon'' subsp. ''tricarpa'' and published the description in ''Contributions from the New South Wales National Herbarium''.{{cite web|title=''Eucalyptus sideroxylon'' subsp. ''tricarpa''|url= https://id.biodiversity.org.au/instance/apni/455146|publisher=APNI|access-date=11 January 2020}} In 1991, Johnson and [[Ken Hill (botanist)|Ken Hill]] raised the subspecies to species level as ''E. tricarpa''.{{cite web|title=''Eucalyptus tricarpa''|url= https://id.biodiversity.org.au/instance/apni/456267|publisher=APNI|access-date=11 January 2020}} The [[Botanical name|specific epithet]] (''tricarpa'') is from [[ancient Greek]] words meaning "three" and "fruit". In 2004, [[Kevin James Rule]] described two subspecies and the names are accepted by the [[Australian Plant Census]]: * ''Eucalyptus tricarpa'' subsp. ''decora'' Rule{{cite web |title=''Eucalyptus tricarpa'' subsp. ''decora'' |url=https://biodiversity.org.au/nsl/services/apc-format/display/191736|website=Australian Plant Census |access-date=11 January 2020}} has [[Pruinescence|pruinose]] seedlings, branchlets, and flower buds;{{cite journal |last1=Rule |first1=Kevin James |title=New taxa in ''Eucalyptus'' (Myrtaceae) for Victoria and notes on Victorian populations of ''Eucalyptus calycogona'' |journal=Muelleria |date=2004 |volume=20 |pages=27–28 |url=https://www.biodiversitylibrary.org/page/59424349#page/29/mode/1up |access-date=29 May 2021}} * ''Eucalyptus tricarpa'' (L.A.S.Johnson) L.A.S.Johnson & K.D.Hill subsp. ''tricarpa'' has no parts that are pruinose. ==Distribution and habitat== ''Eucalyptus tricarpa'' grows in forest and woodland in coastal south from [[Araluen, New South Wales|Araluen]] in New South Wales and is common in the goldfields near [[Bendigo]], near [[Anglesea, Victoria|Anglesea]] and in coastal and near-coastal areas of [[Gippsland]]. Subspecies ''decora'' occurs in open woodland around [[St Arnaud, Victoria|St Arnaud]] in Victoria. {{clear|left}} ==Gallery== {{gallery |title=Features of the red ironbark (''Eucalyptus tricarpa'') |align=center |width=120 |height=120 |style=text-align:center |File:Eucalyptus tricarpa - adult leaves.jpg|Adult leaves |File:Eucalyptus tricarpa - inflorescence.jpg|Inflorescence
